items.stem: An agent passed a single demo run. Why is that insufficient evidence of reliability?

options.text: One success does not measure behaviour across the range of real cases
options.rationale: Correct: reliability needs an evaluation set covering many cases, including failures.

options.text: Demos always use a different model
options.rationale: That is not generally true and not the core issue.
It does not; variance and edge cases remain untested.

options.text: Agents cannot be evaluated at all
options.rationale: They can and should be evaluated.

items.explanation: Correct: reliability needs an evaluation set covering many cases, including failures.

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a robust agent reliability setup? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An evaluation set with objective pass criteria
options.rationale: Correct: objective evals measure task success.

options.text: Post-conditions that block unsafe actions before they reach users
options.rationale: Correct: external checks catch failures the model misses.

options.text: Trusting the model to self-police with no external validation
options.rationale: Self-policing alone is not a guardrail.

options.text: Evaluating only on cases you know pass
options.rationale: Omitting failure cases hides real weaknesses.

items.explanation: Correct: objective evals measure task success.

items.stem: A tool call fails intermittently and the step is NOT safe to repeat. What recovery design is appropriate?

options.text: Fall back to a safe default or human handoff rather than blindly retrying
options.rationale: Correct: unsafe-to-repeat steps need a fallback, not an automatic retry.

options.text: Retry the call immediately as many times as needed
options.rationale: Retrying an unsafe action can cause duplicate side-effects.
Continuing on a failed step risks a bad outcome.
Graceful degradation is preferable to crashing.

items.explanation: Correct: unsafe-to-repeat steps need a fallback, not an automatic retry.
